dialogue.say: The unique four-dish maximum is the baguette, pear, zucchini, and steak; leave the salmon, crab, chicken breast, potato, and quiche plates untouched. Pick up the paring knife on the single large kitchen prep table, cut the pear on the pear plate on that table, and return the knife to that table. Pick up the olive-oil bottle on the single large kitchen prep table, oil the baguette on the baguette plate on that table, the zucchini on the zucchini plate on that table, and the steak on the steak plate on that table, then return the bottle to the prep table.

Keep every clause already completed. If an earlier attempt to put the zucchini onto the frying pan was unstable, pick up that same zucchini where it remains visible beside the frying pan and retry placing it onto the pan; otherwise continue with the first unfinished clause. Turn on the kitchen oven and wait for it to preheat. Open the kitchen oven, pick up the baguette plate from the single large prep table, put the whole plate inside the kitchen oven, and close it. Pick up the zucchini from the zucchini plate on the prep table, put it onto the frying pan on the stove, and turn the stove on. Cook the baguette on the baguette plate inside the closed kitchen oven and the zucchini in the frying pan on the stove; then take the zucchini from the frying pan, return it onto the zucchini plate on the prep table, lift the completed zucchini plate from that table, set it on the metal service counter beside the prep table, and turn the stove off. Leave any completed dish already on the service counter in place, and continue with the next unfinished step.

Keep every clause already completed. If an earlier attempt to put the steak onto the frying pan was unstable, pick up that same steak where it remains visible beside the frying pan and retry placing it onto the pan; otherwise continue with the first unfinished clause. Open the kitchen oven, pick up the completed baguette plate from inside the open kitchen oven, and set it on the metal service counter beside the prep table. From the single large prep table, pick up the pear plate, put the whole plate inside the kitchen oven, and close it. Pick up the steak from the steak plate on the prep table, put it onto the frying pan on the stove, and turn the stove on. Cook the pear on the pear plate inside the closed kitchen oven and the steak in the frying pan on the stove; then return the steak from the frying pan onto the steak plate on the prep table, lift the completed steak plate from that table, and set it on the metal service counter. Leave any completed dish already on the service counter in place, and continue with the next unfinished step.

The pear and steak are now cooked. Turn off the stove and the main kitchen oven, open the main kitchen oven, pick up the completed pear plate inside the open main kitchen oven, set it on the metal service counter beside the prep table, and close the oven.

interaction.public_task_context: Use the inspected menu, thirty-minute limit, one-plate oven, and single stove pan to choose the maximum-cardinality feasible dish set, put every finished plated dish on the metal service counter beside the prep table, leave unchosen dishes untouched, shut down both appliances, and guide execution incrementally.
interaction.human_task_context: You are the wearer and only the Assistant's physical executor, not a second planner. Once the interaction starts, perform no action unless the Assistant's current instruction explicitly requests it; on an idle turn, leave the action empty and ask what to do next. Follow only the currently actionable, single-object step and do exactly what the Assistant says, without choosing, correcting, improving, reordering, or extending its plan. If the current instruction explicitly covers several objects, continue only those named jobs one object per response while that instruction remains active. The motor-object legend, simulator command keys, known-location text, and automatic navigation are grounding aids only; never use them to infer an answer, object location, route, source, or destination that the Assistant did not state. You may directly target a movable only when it is in your current view, it was established by a dedicated earlier inspection, or the Assistant explicitly states its concrete current source location. Its name, command key, or legend entry alone does not qualify, and an incorrect location does not qualify. Otherwise leave the action empty, ask the Assistant where it is, and follow only the room, landmark, navigation, or inspection step the Assistant explicitly gives; never use [Walk], [LookAt], or [Grab] on an unseen object as an automatic-navigation shortcut. Report the observable result after the current instruction is complete, then wait for the next instruction. Never infer completion from score or world state and never end the episode yourself; only the Assistant's dedicated completion token or the action limit ends it.

utterances.say: Hi Assistant, I’ve got thirty minutes, and I want to complete the maximum possible number of dishes from this menu. The oven can take one plate at a time, and I have one pan on the stove. Put every finished dish, on its plate, on the metal service counter beside the prep table, and leave anything we don’t choose untouched. At the end, turn off both appliances and close the oven. Please choose the set, plan the schedule, and guide me one step at a time.
